comment.text: RTKN2 R33 is represented as a recurrently mutated residue in Cancer Hotspots v1. Source observations include Breast carcinoma; Colorectal carcinoma; Glioblastoma; Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma; Cutaneous melanoma. Additional source tumor types are retained in the structured record. Statistical enrichment supports review as a candidate somatic hotspot; it does not establish the functional effect, pathogenicity, or treatment sensitivity of every alteration at this position. This site is present only in the historical V1 material in this collection.

applicability_notes: Confirm the exact allele and reference transcript: source protein numbering is not a validated clinical HGVS assertion.
Tumor counts describe source cohorts and may overlap between releases and sheets; they must not be added together.
An observed synonymous or stop allele is retained for source fidelity and is not automatically classified as oncogenic.
FDA references are separate gene-level evidence until the exact biomarker, tumor, setting, and current label have been checked.

report_comment.text: Somatic alterations affecting RTKN2 residue R33 have been observed in endometrial carcinoma, cutaneous melanoma, and colorectal carcinoma. The functional and clinical significance depend on the specific alteration and tumor type.

comment.text: RTKN2 R33Q is an allele annotation observed in Cancer Hotspots v1 at the R33 hotspot or indel region. This documents recurrence in the source cohorts; allele-specific function, tumor-specific significance, reference-sequence mapping, and clinical actionability require independent review.

report_comment.text: The RTKN2 R33Q alteration has been observed in breast carcinoma and head and neck squamous cell carcinoma. Its functional and clinical significance require allele- and tumor-specific assessment.
